sermon.title: Knowledge of The Bible
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer asks why most Christians in America lack knowledge of the Scriptures. He walks through the bad fruit of the vineyard in Isaiah 5 and God’s way out of captivity in Isaiah 6: letting the old die, seeing Jesus, worshiping, confessing sin and answering “Here I am.” He ends with why Jesus spoke in parables and says understanding comes by coming to Jesus.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: at about 20:54 and 21:44 the captions read “Elijah” for the prophet and servant story of 2 Kings 6:16–17, where the prophet is Elisha; his words are kept. At about 39:34 he says “Ezekiel was given a message to take to the people”; the words he reads (“ever hearing, but never understanding…”) are Isaiah 6:9–10, shown here. He gives “Isaiah 6 1-4” and “second Kings chapter 6 verse 16” in the captions; the other references (Hebrews 12:22, John 4:23, Luke 13:3, John 6:44, Matthew 13, Jeremiah 18:7–8 and others) are named only by his wording and are linked to the matching passages. Where he reads Scripture aloud his wording often differs from the NKJV text shown. In his criticism of American churches he mentions Catholic, Baptist, Pentecostal and charismatic churches, the Latter-day Saints, a music group and a group of “Kansas City prophets” (the last two appear in the transcript only); he comments on homosexuality, abortion and national judgment, and says a country can beat the United States militarily when God intervenes. These are his own views and claims and have not been checked by this site. He names one listener (“Mr. Barnes”) in the transcript only. Spots marked [unclear] include a word before “and drops diamonds” (about 16:38), a place name near “Acts 2 or someone in…” (about 26:30), and three phrases at about 40:26, 41:25 and 43:14. “Hillsong” and the first-century Bible names were spelled from the captions.

chunks.section_question: Why does he say most Christians in America lack knowledge of the Scriptures? (Isaiah 5)
chunks.short_answer: He opens by saying “most Christians in America have no understanding of the scriptures at all,” and that if we know why, “we can, what, reverse it and get knowledge of the scriptures.” He says Isaiah 5 shows that we, the people of God, are his vineyard, “a parable, an allegory, a metaphor of the truth of God’s word,” and that this vineyard is producing bad fruit.

And if we know why we don’t have knowledge of the scriptures, then we can, what, reverse it and get knowledge of the scriptures. Hallelujah. And you just try to figure out right now the answer. Just say in your mind, “I think I got the answer to that,” and then see how it matches up at the end, when you get God’s answer. Is that a good one? Yeah, all right. Yeah, you know, you need to learn how to get involved in these things. All right, so we go to Isaiah chapter 5, and here God is going to talk about his vineyard, and he told us in Isaiah 5 that we, the people of God, are his vineyard. See, so the vineyard is a parable, an allegory, a metaphor of the truth of God’s word.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about tyranny and social programs replacing justice and righteousness? (Isaiah 5:7)
chunks.short_answer: He names the first bad fruit as replacing justice with oppression: “instead of justice we have oppression, we have tyranny,” with church leaders who “do nothing but manipulate the people,” when Jesus is the real shepherd. The second is replacing righteousness with welfare; he says “the church has not been given social programs,” and that turning people “to righteousness and to justice” is “their priority job.”
chunks.text:
Number one, they replace justice with oppression, with tyranny. You don’t know, they want to dictate their own life, they want to dictate everybody else’s life to conform to them. Instead of justice we have oppression, we have tyranny, and we’ve got a lot of church leaders that do nothing but manipulate the people. They’re tyrants. It’s their way or the highway, they just lead. You know, who is our real leader? Jesus Christ. Who’s the real shepherd? Jesus Christ. All the rest of us are under-shepherds, we’re just delegated people, and we need to get off our high horse and point people to the real what? Shepherd. All right, Jesus knows how to lead and rule over us and give us the freedom to choose. Amen. And his ways are always right.

Number two, they cry for help instead of righteousness. They replace righteousness with welfare. Most churches in America are on a social, a community social, uh, uh, program: helping the poor, ministering to the, uh, drug rehabilitation. Uh, our, our United States government, by the way, has over 70 social welfare programs, I think it’s 79 main ones. See, we replace doing right with [unclear] them to do wrong. Are you out there? Okay. Social programs, and boy, if you’re helping the drug addict and you’re helping the poor and the, and the homeless and all that, oh, what a Christian you are. And without righteousness you’re not beans. I don’t care if you help the poor or not. Justice and righteousness are high principles in God’s word, and when the church is preaching the gospel and turning people to righteousness and to justice, they’re doing their priority job, whether they ever do anything else or not. The church has not been given social programs. Right? But every church on TV and the big popular ones, that’s all they push is social programs. That was a good amen, but anyway, it might have went over your head.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about music, intoxication and calling evil good? (Isaiah 5:11-12, 20)

These are his views.
chunks.text:
We need God, and we need the power of God in the church, and we need the gospel of righteousness and justice. Could that be an amen? Doing right, doing just, doing, that’s what’s going to bless your home, bless your life, bless your children. Number three, intoxication and music. Boy, is he, is he seeing the American church right now, thousands of years before we ever existed? This is the American church overall, most of the churches. This is it: it’s okay to drink, get intoxicated, and the world’s music. In fact, bring the world’s music in and we’ll come to church, and your seeker-friendly churches are built on pleasing you. So you like country music, we’ll have country music, and we’ll have all the seekers that seek country music to come. You like rock music, we’ll have rock music, we get all the rock people to come. That isn’t Bible. Are you out there?

And America is drugged on music and intoxication. They go together. “Give me a beer and give me a song,” ain’t that right? And then they call themselves believers, and God says the vineyard is producing bad fruit. They call evil good and good evil. Wow, isn’t that what we’re doing in America? They’re saying homosexuality, “God made them that way, and it’s an acceptable lifestyle.” They’re calling what God said is evil, good. Isn’t that what America is doing? Killing innocent babies in the womb because they don’t have self-control to begin with, making it a contraceptive on demand. No Jesus, no Bible is accepted in public places. Jesus is good, the Bible is good, and they call that evil. Is that America? Absolutely.

chunks.text:
Wise in their own eyes. They’re wise in their own eyes. Everybody thinks, “Well, I believe.” Isn’t that the famous statement of most Christians in America? “Well, I believe it this way.” And because they believe it, it’s supposed to be. Okay, we’re supposed to believe what God told us to believe. Amen. We can’t add to the word. I can’t go and say, “Well, Lord, you said this way, but this is the way I see it. Now bless me. It’s the captivity to bad fruit, it’s the captivity of sin. Didn’t Jesus say, “They that serve sin is the slave of sin”? And a slave is a what? A captive. They’re forced against their own will. Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: Why does he say the old thing must die before God brings the new? (Isaiah 6:1)
chunks.short_answer: He says “the year King Uzziah died” teaches that “there has to be a death of the old thing before the bringing in of the new thing,” and he gives Saul and David, Moses and Joshua, and Jesus and the church as examples. He says “we got to stay in the new thing,” that he does not want to “resurrect the dead horse,” and that the revival of the late ’40s to the ’70s has died.
chunks.text:
Now then, God always in the scriptures gives us a way out. He always does, because that’s who he is. God’s way of avoiding captivity. How many don’t want to go into captivity? Captivity just sounds bad, doesn’t it? Even if you don’t understand it scripturally, it just sounds bad. You don’t want to be a slave of anything, let alone sin. Here’s God’s way of avoiding captivity. All right, first, in Isaiah 6:1-4, “the year King Uzziah died.” You say, “Well, what in the world, what’s that got to do with anything?” Well, if you know your Bible and remember all things were written for our learning, our admonition, you see, our examples. And so it is important that this statement is understood: there has to be a death of the old thing before the bringing in of the new thing.

It’s all through the Bible. Remember Saul, and King Saul and David? King Saul was evil, had an evil spirit. David was a man after God’s own heart and appointed by God to be king, but it wouldn’t happen until what? Saul was dead. Are you there? Remember Moses, see, God promised to bring him into the land, but they couldn’t go into the land till Moses died, and then Joshua, the new thing, God, the fresh thing God was doing, moved them into the land. Are you out there? Okay, let’s look at Jesus. Jesus had to die before the church was raised up, before the new thing. Are you there? Hallelujah. The Bible says that we got to die to ourself before we can get in the thing God’s doing. “If any man be in Christ, he is a” what? “New creation. Old things are passed away, all things are become new.”

And church, listen to me, we got to stay in the new thing, and the word new just means the fresh thing, it’s what God is doing. It may be an old thing that God has brought up to make it a fresh thing. We don’t even think when we pray that God may be up to something new, and I happen to know he is, and I don’t know what it is, but I know he’s up to something. And I don’t want to be trying to resurrect the dead horse when he’s got a live one ready for me to train and ride. Hallelujah. Now, that was good, I’m just letting that sink into you. God’s got to do this thing in you, and so we need the death of the old thing. The revival, the awakening of the late ‘40s to the ‘70s has died. I don’t know if you know it, it’s died. Okay, I’m just going to tell you, it’s dead.

And what are we doing? We’re trying to hang on to the past, and God is wanting to blow a fresh and do a new thing, and we need to be looking to what? The fresh new thing. Can I hear an amen? Hallelujah. People still want to do what they did years ago when God is wanting to bring something new. Wow, that was is good. So you see, this is an important statement. When you read your Bible, you just go, “Oh, the king died,” and you go on, you don’t even think that God is trying to tell you something. Now you know he is. Amen. Didn’t, doesn’t the Bible say that there had to be the death of the Old Testament for the birth of the New Testament? Didn’t he? Yeah, he said the Old Testament’s done away with and the New Testament is here. Most Christians cannot tell me what the New Testament is, and it’s powerful. You should have that memorized. Is that challenging? Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: Why does he say we must see Jesus, and what does he say about angels with wings? (Isaiah 6:1-2)
chunks.short_answer: He says “we got to get our eyes off of ministers,” great speakers and big churches, because they distract from Jesus, and “we got to get our eyes on Jesus Christ.” He says angels don’t have wings, only seraphim and cherubim do, and that stories of feathers or jewels appearing in church “ain’t Bible.”
chunks.text:
Now the next thing that’s got to happen is we got to see Jesus. “I saw the Lord sitting on the throne, high and lifted up, and the train,” the tail of the train, the Lord, part of his robe filled the temple. We couldn’t handle it all, so he just let the lower part come in. Folks, we got to see Jesus. We got, we got to get our eyes off of ministers, we got to get our eyes off of great speakers, we got to get our eyes off big churches. Whatever our eyes are on that’s distracting us from Jesus. And a lot of us have just got our eyes on ourselves. We only care about ourselves, we get up in the morning to please ourselves. We got to get our eyes on Jesus Christ. It’s not the Baptist church, it’s not the independent church, it’s not the Catholic church, it’s not the Presbyterian church, it’s not the people that hate church, it’s Jesus we got to see.

And he wants to reveal himself to us. I got to see Jesus, and I got to see he’s on the throne, he is Lord, and if I’m going to serve him, I got to be his slave. Amen. I got to be his citizen. I got to quit looking to ministers, I got to quit looking to groups, I got to quit looking to books and tapes, and I got to go to Jesus Christ. That’s imperative, because without him you can do what? Nothing. Nothing. Say it: nothing. Nothing. And yet we try to all the time.

Now, the seraphim, those, those winged creatures in heaven. Angels don’t have wings. I’ve been trying to correct the church world for 40 years. You know, women decorate their house with angels with wings, not in the Bible. The angels don’t have wings. Seraphim and cherubim have wings, angels don’t have wings. And these, these false churches, Pentecostals that I am in, charismatic tongue-talkers, they say, “God visited us and a feather was left from the wing.” I go, “That’s stupid. Angels don’t have wings, how can they leave a feather? You put the feather there.” It’s true. I mean, I have to, I have to have, I got to solve these things, people call me.

And you know, and then they have jewels appearing, you know, “God comes through with his [unclear] and drops diamonds and precious stones all around.” That ain’t Bible. We’re the stones that he’s interested in. He’s not interested in diamonds, he wants to make a diamond out of you, idiot. And us tongue-talkers, I tell you, we got some weirdos in the Spirit-filled church circle, I tell you, we got some real hamdingers, but you non-spiritual people got some hamdingers of your own. Amen. Yeah. And gullible people that don’t know the gospel believe this stuff, get caught up, especially women. They have something about women, they want to get into the sensationalism instead of the truth.

chunks.section_question: Why does he say we must become worshipers? (Hebrews 12:22, John 4:23)
chunks.short_answer: He says the seraphim cry “holy, holy, holy,” and the Bible says we have come to “an innumerable company of angels,” so we join them in lifting our voices. chunks.text:
And these seraphim are crying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts. chunks.section_question: What does “the whole earth is full of his glory” mean, and how much time should we give God? (2 Kings 6:16-17)
chunks.short_answer: He tells of Elisha’s servant who saw an enemy army around the city while Elisha saw more with them; when God opened the servant’s eyes there were “chariots of fire” all around. He says “the glory of the Lord is truly here, you just need your eyes open to see it,” and asks people to give God “one hour a day,” with the word, prayer and worship working together.
chunks.text:
So we got to worship, we got to see Jesus, and we got to die to ourselves, and we got to die to the past, whatever that is. “The whole earth is full of his glory. The whole earth is full of his glory.” Wow. Is the whole earth full of his glory? It’s prophetic. Doesn’t the Bible say that the glory of the Lord shall fill the earth as the waters cover the sea? That’s in the future, but here he’s saying the whole earth is full of his glory. What in the world does that mean? 2 Kings chapter 6, verse 16. Elisha is in a city with his servant. They get up in the morning, and the servant goes out on the city wall, and behold, the army of the enemy has surrounded the town. The servant runs back to the man of God, the prophet Elisha, and said, “Elijah, we’re surrounded! What are we going to do? We’re in big trouble!”

And Elisha looked at his servant and says, “No, no, we’re not in trouble. There’s more for us than there is with them.” The servant goes, “Elisha, have you look, come, come on, use your eyes, use your common sense, there’s an army out there all around the city, we’re doomed.” He didn’t see the glory of the Lord. Elisha saw the glory of the Lord, and Elisha said, “Lord, open his eyes, open his eyes to see your glory,” and God opened the eyes of the servant, and behold, chariots of fire were all around Elijah, and the army of heaven, the angels, were all around that army on earth. The glory of the Lord is truly here, you just need your eyes open to see it. Wow. And that’s worth missing TV at night for. We got all this time for what we think is important.

And we wonder why we don’t see the glory. Because we don’t put God, ask for one hour a day. I was teaching the young people this week, one hour a day. He’s not, and then one day a week, he, that’s for one hour a day and one day a week, and we can’t even give him 60 minutes a day, and then we wonder why we don’t have anything to contribute. Are you there? Hallelujah. How many raise your hand and say, “I’m going to bust my butt to give God one hour a day”? That’s the word, prayer, and worship, the three work together. See, the word is where you get truth and understand it, it’s the worship and the prayer that the Spirit ignites it, and the Spirit gives you revelation of what you read. It’s a, it’s an important team. “The whole earth is full of his glory.”

chunks.section_question: Why does he say we need a demonstration of God’s glory today? (Acts 2, Acts 4)
chunks.short_answer: He says that in the Bible God’s glory “was a demonstration of his power,” “some kind of verbal, audible, visible demonstration,” and points to the rushing wind and tongues of fire in Acts 2 and the shaking in Acts 4. He asks, “is it possible he’s got a fresh glory to reveal to his present-day church?” and says to pray “God, shake us the way you want to shake us today” and to “break away from yesterday.”
chunks.text:
Hallelujah. “Their voices shook, and smoke filled the house.” So the house, the temple of God, was shaken, and the house was filled with smoke. The glory, we, we understand that in the Bible, when God revealed his glory, it was a demonstration of his power. It was some kind of verbal, audible, visible demonstration. And folks, we need the glory of God, we need a demonstration of God, not just thinking in our minds, but we need a demonstration to hit us and experience. Now in Acts chapter 2, remember, they, 120 were in the upper room, a mighty wind came through, a rushing mighty wind, that was a noise, that was a noise, and then tongues of fire came, and then they spoke in the languages of that day the mighty works of God. See, there was a visible demonstration of the glory of God.

When the wind blew, you could see it, they had to hold their coats on, and it was a rushing, it was a noisy wind, and the people weren’t doing anything yet. They weren’t making noise, I mean, they were praying, but it wasn’t a noise, didn’t come from them, it came from heaven. And then fire, tongues of fire lit on each one. Why are we so skeptic of a supernatural God doing supernatural things in America? Is God the same yesterday, today, and forever? If he did that for the early church, can he do things for the present-day church? Does he want just to repeat the rushing wind and tongues of fire, or is it possible he’s got a fresh glory to reveal to his present-day church? It’s very possible. We haven’t seen things yet that God can do in our generation.

Then you go over to Acts 4. They’re in there praying, and they’re all praying audibly, and they were praying that God would grant unto them that signs and wonders would be done by the hands of the apostles. Then the place was shaken, and they spoke the word of God with confidence, and sure enough, the apostles did great signs and wonders. They asked for it, they got it. There was a, there was a witness that God heard their prayers by the shaking and by them having the confidence to speak the word. Are you there? Hallelujah. And church, we need a shaking, and we don’t need to be looking like it’s going to happen like it did in Acts 4 or in Acts 2 or someone in [unclear] or somewhere else. We just need to say, “God, shake us the way you want to shake us today.” Amen.

See, reveal yourself to us the way you want to reveal yourself to us today. You are a supernatural God, we are not going to limit you to our feeble mentality. You do, here we are, Lord, you do what you want to do. Is that a good attitude? Yeah. We got to break away from yesterday. You got to break away from the Baptist, from the Pentecostal, from the charismatic, from the Catholics. You got to break away and see this man Jesus and get into his glory and be a vessel of that glory. Wow, that was good stuff.

chunks.section_question: What was Isaiah’s response to the glory, and why does he say repentance is the main message? (Isaiah 6:5)
chunks.short_answer: He says that after the glory came, Isaiah’s response was that “he confessed his sins,” and “you got to admit you’re wrong.” He says “repentance is the main message,” the first message of John the Baptist and of Jesus, who said “unless you repent you will all likewise perish.” He says Isaiah “had talked wrong,” and tells people to stop justifying and making excuses.
chunks.text:
Church, God’s way of avoiding captivity always has this one. Isaiah is a prophet, okay, he’s a holy man, he’s a man that’s in tune with God, hears what God is saying, and yet when the glory of God shook the place and shook Isaiah, and the revelation of the smoke of God, the glory filled the place, this is Isaiah’s response. Who? “Hey, I saw the glory! I saw the glory! Get me on TV, get me on TV, man! Oh yeah, put me out on tape, get me out on tape, I saw the glory, I saw the glory!” That’s what us Pentecostals do. We get a little visitation and we go bragging about what we experience and we miss the whole message. And you non-Pentecostals, you didn’t even see, so don’t be bragging. Are you there?

Now, here’s Isaiah’s response to the glory, to the dying of the king, the new thing coming, the worship. This is his response to the whole thing after the glory came: he confessed his sins. Church, this is the key. You got to admit you’re wrong when you know God says it’s wrong. Just admit it. Good Lord, stop justifying. Many of us spend hours justifying our failures to others instead of just humbly saying, “I’m wrong, I got to change this.” It’s not, “My husband made me do it,” or “my wife made me do it,” or “my children drive me crazy,” or “my parents are driving me crazy,” or “the community is driving me crazy,” or “the school’s driving me crazy.” Stop justifying your error. Just admit you’re wrong. And a lot of us, “Well, the way I was raised,” oh, cut it out. The power of the blood of Christ is higher than the way you were raised.

“Oh, it’s my daddy was that way, and my mama was that way, and I’m that way, and the grandpa was that way, all of us are that way.” Oh, get off of it. You’re just making excuses for staying dumb. Repentance. What was the first message John the Baptist preached? What was the only message John the Baptist preached in the coming of Christ? Yeah. What was the first message Jesus preached? Repentance. What do these mega churches and everybody tell you? Faith and grace, you don’t have to repent. And yet Jesus said, “Unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.” Jesus said that. Unless you repent, unless you turn from your sin, unless you admit you’re wrong and turn from it, and if you mess up, you get up and you admit it and turn from it again, you’re going to be destroyed.

Repentance is the main message. Turning from wrong to what? Right. Turning from the kingdom of darkness to the kingdom of light, turning from Satan to Jesus Christ. That’s what it is, it’s that simple. And the key to it is admitting you’re wrong and turning from the wrong, and God will cleanse you, forgive you, erase the record. Isn’t that powerful? “Woe to me!” Isaiah cried. “Woe to me, I’m in trouble, I am ruined, I’m a man of unclean lips, and I’ve lived among a people of unclean lips, and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord God Almighty.” I’m in big trouble. See, he hadn’t committed adultery, he hadn’t stolen anything, he hadn’t dishonored his parents, he hadn’t worshiped idols, but he had talked wrong. And if Isaiah needed to confess and repent, don’t we?

chunks.section_question: How does he say a person is cleansed and sent? (Isaiah 6:6-8)
chunks.short_answer: He says “there’s only one church anyway, and that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ,” and that the coal touching Isaiah’s lip shows you repent “until heaven comes and touches you and cleanses you, and that’s what we call being born again.” When God asks whom to send, he says we can’t be “non-involved Christians,” and the prayer to pray is “Here I am, use me.”
chunks.text:
And this is the foundation of having the glory of God come to you and having your eyes open to see Jesus: you got to admit you’re wrong. And a lot of us have a lot more to confess than the way we talk, and the way we talk isn’t good. The Bible says let everything be done to edifying, and we tear everybody down. Ain’t that right? Bible tells us to bridle our tongue, and we just tell everybody off. “Take that! That’s it, the way I am.” We commit idolatry by greed, we get drunk, intoxicated, we have sexual relationships outside of our marriage, we do all this stuff, and we think we’re going to go to heaven because of faith and grace, and, and these ministers have lied to you. I’m just going to tell you, they’re lying to you. You go to the Bible, it was repentance, turning from wrong to right.

I don’t care if you’re Catholic, Baptist, Pentecost, I don’t care what you are. I don’t care about the tag outside, or you’re just a non-church person. Nobody can be a non-church person, by the way. God has ordained that we assemble together to provoke one another to love and to good works and to exhort one another. We need to be reminded to live right. Isn’t that right? We don’t need to be told, “You’re okay the way you are.” No, the church is supposed to assemble together to build character and maintain character. I don’t care what group you’re in, there’s only one church anyway, and that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ. And that’s not the Latter-day Saints, that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ. You’re born into it, you’re birthed into it. I don’t care what the title is out on the door. Throw away the titles.

And then what? The angel brought a coal from the fire, the altar of heaven, touched his lip, took away the guilt, cleansed his lip, and atoned for his sin. See, you repent until God births repentance, forgiveness in you. Till heaven touches you, you can’t get a baptismal certificate, or a church membership card, or whatever, I ain’t going to do anything, but you repent, you confess your wrong until heaven comes and touches you and cleanses you, and that’s what we call being born again. Are you there? Hallelujah.

Now, so now we’re delivered from captivity. After being delivered from captivity, what’s next on God’s agenda? Hallelujah. “Whom shall I send to these people in captivity?” See, he is free now. He’s not going into captivity, he’s not in captivity, he’s free, and now God says, “Whom am I going to send to these people in captivity?” Does God always care for the people in captivity? Yes. Yes, church, he does. He’s always interested in them, but he has principles. Somebody’s got to go and talk to them. See, we can’t sit back and be non-involved Christians. We can’t be so worried about offending people that we are silenced by public opinion: keep your religion to yourself.

Why is it that every subject’s okay to talk about but Jesus Christ? Because Jesus Christ brings conviction, and you either get mad or you get glad, one of the two. There’s no neutral reaction here. It’s always, they are mad because they don’t want to change their ways and they don’t want to hear you, or they’re glad because, “Hey, thank you for showing me the way.” The response of Isaiah, who is now cleansed, delivered, atoned for, says, “Here I am. I’m atoned for, I’m clean, I’m forgiven. Here I am, use me. I don’t know what to do, but here I am, use me.” Do you ever pray that prayer?

Prayer in America, the, the prayers I hear, I hear this all the time: “God help me, God help me, God help me, God help me.” For 30 years people have been praying the same prayer. “God help me, God help me, God help me, help me to be a prayer, help me to be a worshiper.” Is God the hindrance here? No. We need to respond and say, “Here I am, use me. Make me a prayer, make me a worshiper, make me one that can speak the word of God with confidence.” But that requires responsibility to speak the word, you got to read the word. “Oh my gosh, I got to miss the soap operas, that’s a, that’s a big price. I’m going to miss my kid’s soccer game.” “Here I am.” What can you say? “Here I am, send me.” Let me hear it: “Here I am, send me.” Yes.

chunks.section_question: What message did God give Isaiah to preach, and for how long? (Isaiah 6:9-12)
chunks.short_answer: He says God’s message was “be ever hearing” but “never understanding,” and that “it’s not your responsibility whether they listen or not, it’s your responsibility to speak the word of God.” When Isaiah asks how long, God says until the cities lie ruined, which he takes to mean the Babylonian captivity, “then he gives an exception.” He attributes this message to Ezekiel; see the editor note.
chunks.text:
Don’t be afraid to speak with fortitude, church. Guys, we sing some of our songs so wimpy. “I’m a child of the King” isn’t a wimpy song, that is a prophetic song. “I am his, royal blood flows.” Sing it like that. Could that be an amen? “Go and tell these people.” “Okay, here I am, use me.” You got to go and you got to do something. “But Lord, it’s embarrassing to tell people about God Almighty, and the public opinion is keep your religion to yourself.” That’s America. chunks.section_question: Who are the tenth, the holy seed that escape captivity? (Isaiah 6:13)
chunks.short_answer: He says “though a tenth remain in the land,” and to be in that tenth you must die to the old, get in the new, become a worshiper and seek Jesus. He says “it’s righteousness that will protect you in any judgment or visitation of God,” that “repentance to do right, not faith in grace” escapes captivity, and that “the key is the word repent.” He says God “cuts us down to size, and then he starts growing us again.”
chunks.text:
Church, everyone’s supposed to go far away, and everybody wants to take the word of God literally without balancing it out with the whole word of God. He’s going to give us an exception, all right. “Though a tenth remain in the land, it will be laid waste, but as trees leave stumps when cut down, so” how many is going to be left in the land? 10%. How many want to be part of the 10 [unclear]? Well, to be that part, you got to follow what we just taught, what Isaiah was revealed. You need to die to the old, get in the new, hallelujah, become a worshiper, look for Jesus, seek him. Now the tenth, the tenth, so the holy seed will be the stump in the land.

I told you in the last message, it’s righteousness. It’s not being a Catholic, a Baptist, or Pentecostal or whatever, it’s righteousness that will protect you in any judgment or visitation of God. You don’t have to be a preacher, you don’t have to speak in tongues, you don’t have to prophesy, you don’t have to lead one soul to Christ. If you’re living righteous, God’s going to honor you, and by the way, if you are living righteous, he’s going to make you a fisher of men. The two go together. The holy seed. So repentance to do right, not faith in grace, that’s the one that’s going to escape the captivity. And when God judges America, and the road America’s on, on, I’m speaking this prophetically, by history and by the Bible, the road America’s on, God’s going to intervene. And I told you, Mexico can beat us militarily when God intervenes.

Nobody and no army can protect you when God decides that a nation needs to be humbled. Are you there? Remember, Jeremiah said, “When the Lord has determined judgment upon a nation, upon a people, if they will turn and repent, he will turn from the judgment.” So we can, what? Change this road we’re on, and the key is the word repent. Say it: repent. People in America need to turn from their wrong and do right. 1 Corinthians 13. You know that us Pentecostals, because we speak in tongues and prophesy and get a word of knowledge sometimes, and, you know, we see, go, God healed the sick and all that. 1 Corinthians 13 is very clear, though: “Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels and have not love, I’m nothing. Though I can prophesy and have faith to move mountains and do miracles and have not love, I’m nothing. Though I give my body to be burned, and though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor,” all these social programs that we’re into, drug rehabilitation, alcohol rehabilitation, prostitute rehabilitation, divorce rehab, all these social programs, “without love it profits me nothing.”

God will cut us down, God will trim us, God will correct us, but any stump left will start growing into a tree again. Hallelujah. See, when the tree is wrong and the fruit’s wrong, God cuts it down. He doesn’t cut us out, he cuts us down to size, and then he starts growing us again. How many could use a regrowth? Yeah, yeah. Isn’t this powerful?

chunks.short_answer: He says God “doesn’t need blood moons or anything to consummate the end time,” only “Jesus coming through that cloud.” He tells hearers “don’t believe that garbage,” calls it “salesmanship,” and says he told a Pentecostal in China that people following such prophets were following “false prophets.” These are his opinions about unnamed groups and have not been verified here.

chunks.short_answer: He says the disciples asked why Jesus spoke in parables, and the answer is “it has been given you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.” He says “whoever has, to him more will be given,” and that what the disciples had was “a response of heart”: they repented, believed and followed, so they got more.

We find it in the New Testament. Okay, New Testament use of Isaiah chapter 6. “Why do you speak to them in” what? Say the word: parables. Remember, he speaks through shadow, laws, parables, metaphors, allegories, you know, uh, a historical report of Israel. He speaks to us through all these things. And so the disciples are saying, “Why do you speak to the people in parables? Why don’t you just say directly what you want to say?” Are you there? Are you with me so far? Yeah. Why did God use parables? Why did he just say what he wanted to say? “Because it has been given you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.”

Okay, he says, “You apostles, it’s been given to you to know the mysteries.” So are there secrets and mysteries hidden in the Bible? Yeah, the Bible says that, we taught you that before. Okay, why would God hide these things in the word? Why would he do that? Is that a good question? Why can’t I just open the book and, bang, I just get it? And, may, read Leviticus the first time and go, “Oh man, this is boring.” That was me. I couldn’t wait to get through it, it was torture going through Leviticus, just torture. Now when I go through Leviticus, bam! “For whoever has,” what’s the word? Has. What, what do these apostles have, these disciples have, that the other people didn’t have?

You see, “whoever has, to him more will be given, and he will have” what? “Abundance. But whoever does not have,” what, don’t they have? “Even that which he has will be taken away from him.” So the one who has keeps having more, and the one who doesn’t have loses even that which he had. When Jesus came to the apostles and said, “Follow me,” they just dropped everything and followed him. They responded. See, they didn’t have authority over sicknesses and demons at that time, they had a responsive heart.

chunks.section_question: How does he say we can understand the Bible? (John 6:44, Matthew 13:13-15)
chunks.short_answer: He says “the word of God is beyond human intellect,” and that the answer is to come to Jesus, humble yourself and say “Lord, open my eyes, open my understanding.” He says “the Holy Ghost is what opens your eyes,” that American people lack knowledge of the scriptures “because they don’t humble themselves, come to Jesus,” and he urges listening to messages “on your knees.”
chunks.text:
Didn’t Jesus say, “No man comes to me except the Father draw him, and no man comes to the Father but by me”? You can’t skirt, see, the revelation of God’s word, the drawing of his Spirit, by human intellect. And God knows that those that come to him, then they are candidates to be revealed the parables and healed and set free. Are you there? See, the word of God is beyond human intellect. If you keep it in the human intellect, you’re not going to understand that Bible. But when you come to Jesus and humble yourself and say, “God, open my understanding, open my eyes,” he will. I can remember when parables of the New Testament were opened to me. I can remember the day, bam, God came, because I didn’t understand those parables, things didn’t make sense to me, and bam, and once I understood the key parable, I understood them all, and then the New Testament just opened up tremendously, just like the Old Testament, in shadow, laws, and, and, uh, historical events of Israel, just revelation came. faqs.question: What does he say the vineyard represents in the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says Isaiah 5 shows “we, the people of God, are his vineyard,” and that when the Bible mentions the vineyard “he’s talking about what? The church,” unless it specifically says “a wild vineyard,” which is about sin.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, And the men of Judah are His pleasant plant. He looked for justice, but behold, oppression; For righteousness, but behold, a cry for help.

faqs.question: What does he say it means that we know people by their fruit?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus said “you know them by their fruit,” so “your works are important, what you do and what you say is important.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: You will know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes from thornbushes or figs from thistles?

faqs.question: Who does he say the real leader and shepherd is?
faqs.answer: He says it is Jesus Christ, and that “all the rest of us are under-shepherds, we’re just delegated people” who need to “get off our high horse” and point people to him.

faqs.question: What does he say matters without righteousness?
faqs.answer: He says “without righteousness you’re not beans,” and that “justice and righteousness are high principles in God’s word.” He says the church’s “priority job” is preaching the gospel and turning people to righteousness and justice.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, And the men of Judah are His pleasant plant. He looked for justice, but behold, oppression; For righteousness, but behold, a cry for help.

faqs.question: What does he say “the year King Uzziah died” has to do with us?
faqs.answer: He says “all things were written for our learning,” and that the king’s death shows “there has to be a death of the old thing before the bringing in of the new thing.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and the train of His robe filled the temple.
Now all these things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come.

faqs.question: What examples does he give of the old dying before the new?
faqs.answer: He gives Saul and David (“David was a man after God’s own heart”), Moses and Joshua, and Jesus, who “had to die before the church was raised up.” He adds that “we got to die to ourself,” and quotes “if any man be in Christ” as being a new creation.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

faqs.question: Does he say angels have wings?
faqs.answer: He says no: “angels don’t have wings. Seraphim and cherubim have wings.” He says he has been trying to correct this for 40 years.

faqs.question: What does he say about praying in secret during corporate worship?
faqs.answer: He says “worship isn’t the time to be secret, and corporate prayer is not a time to be in your closet. It’s an attitude.” He says “I’m not praying for people to hear, I’m praying to my God.”

faqs.question: How much time with God does he say we should give each day?
faqs.answer: He asks people to give God “one hour a day,” and says “the word, prayer, and worship, the three work together,” with the Spirit giving “revelation of what you read.”

faqs.question: What does he say about making excuses for our failures?
faqs.answer: He says “stop justifying your error. Just admit you’re wrong,” and that “the power of the blood of Christ is higher than the way you were raised.”

faqs.question: Does he say a person can be a “non-church person”?
faqs.answer: He says “nobody can be a non-church person,” because God has ordained that we “assemble together to provoke one another to love and to good works.” He says “there’s only one church anyway, and that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

faqs.question: Why does he say people avoid talking about Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says every subject is okay to talk about but Jesus Christ “because Jesus Christ brings conviction and you either get mad or you get glad, one of the two.”

faqs.question: What does he say about the prayer “God help me”?
faqs.answer: He says people have prayed “God help me” for 30 years, and asks “is God the hindrance here? No.” He says we need to respond, “Here I am, use me.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying: “Whom shall I send, And who will go for Us?” Then I said, “Here am I! Send me.”

faqs.question: What does he say 1 Corinthians 13 teaches about works without love?
faqs.answer: Reading 1 Corinthians 13, he says that even tongues, prophecy, faith that moves mountains and giving to the poor are nothing “without love it profits me nothing.” He applies it to social programs and rehabilitation work.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing. Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil;

faqs.question: What does he say about a tree that God cuts down to a stump?
faqs.answer: He says “God will cut us down, God will trim us, God will correct us, but any stump left will start growing into a tree again.” He says God “doesn’t cut us out, he cuts us down to size, and then he starts growing us again.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But yet a tenth will be in it, And will return and be for consuming, As a terebinth tree or as an oak, Whose stump remains when it is cut down. So the holy seed shall be its stump.”
